name: Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinoses

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinoses

criteria.description: Progressive neurodegeneration with seizures, vision loss, and cognitive decline
Detection of characteristic autofluorescent lipopigment accumulation in biopsied tissue
Identification of pathogenic variants in NCL-associated genes (e.g., CLN1, CLN2, CLN3)
MRI showing cerebral and cerebellar atrophy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive neurodegenerative clinical features plus either characteristic ultrastructural findings or pathogenic genetic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by genetic testing and/or electron microscopy of tissue samples.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive vision loss due to retinal degeneration

common.symptomName: Behavioral disturbances including irritability and aggression

laboratory: Elevated lysosomal storage material in leukocytes
Autofluorescent lipopigment accumulation in skin or conjunctival biopsy
imaging: MRI showing cerebral and cerebellar atrophy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in CLN1, CLN2, CLN3, and other NCL-related genes
other: Electron microscopy revealing fingerprint or granular osmiophilic deposits in lysosomes

distinguishingFeatures: Muscle biopsy showing ragged red fibers
CAG repeat expansion in HTT gene

redFlags: Rapidly progressive vision loss in a child
references: Mole SE, Williams RE, Goebel HH. The Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinoses (Batten Disease). Oxford University Press; 2011.
Williams RE, Mole SE. New nomenclature and classification scheme for the neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses. Neurology. 2012;79(2):183-191.
The National Organization for Rare Disorders (NORD). Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinoses. 2020.
